text:
maria: pushed a dashboard update to surface prefix cache hit-rate by model/route/customer — link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ABC123/prefix-hitrate (pls don't share outside eng)
sam: saw the alert. which metric dropped? hit-rate or token-saved?
maria: hit-rate. chat-stream-v2 for customer=AcmeCorp dropped ~72% -> 56% starting 03/12 14:10 UTC after the runtime deploy. tokens_saved/day also down ~40% -> 25k.
jess: any model-specific pattern? single model or across models?
maria: mostly rw-open-13b and rw-open-7b on that route. other routes for AcmeCorp unchanged.
kai: can we rule out batching/kernel-changes from the deploy? last deploy touched kernel-selection heuristics and seq-boundary trimming.
sam: i ran a quick trace. KC (kv cache) lookups spiked but hit ratio dropped — looks like lookup keys are more variable now. suspect key canonicalization change in PR #489.
maria: here are two example keys (from sampled logs):
```
user:acme:conv:1234|normalize:v1|prompthash:abcd1234
user:acme:conv:1234 | normalize:v1 | prompthash:abcd1234
```
notice the whitespace variant. earlier normalization collapsed spaces; new path keeps original spacing when caller includes trailing spaces.
henry: that smells like a subtle normalizer refactor. PR note said "preserve original tokens for better traceability" — unintended side-effect.
observability-bot: alert fired: prefix_cache_hitrate_drop(customer="AcmeCorp", route="chat-stream-v2") at 2026-03-12T14:30:12Z :eyes:
jess: short triage plan: 1) confirm PR ownership and repro locally 2) run kv-key-diff for AcmeCorp 3) if confirmed, roll a hotfix to restore previous normalizer or add a normalization shim at routing layer.
kai: i can run a 6-hour sampling job that computes key-entropy and collision rate per-model. query i'll use:
```
# Grafana / PromQL-ish
sum by(customer, route, model) (rate(prefix_cache_hits[1h])) / sum by(customer, route, model) (rate(prefix_cache_lookups[1h]))
```
will also emit token_savings breakdown.
sam: we should be careful — kernel batching changes could also change prefix lengths seen by the cache when requests are chunked differently. but the whitespace examples make normalizer first suspect.
maria: assigning: kai -> sampling + eviction/entropy; sam -> kernel/batching quick-check; jess -> coord with PR owner and prod-rollback plan; i'll coordinate with AcmeCorp SE.
henry: temporary mitigation we can flip feature flag: `prefetch.normalizer=v0` for customer AcmeCorp via admin console. that should restore old canonicalization without full rollback.
jess: good. let's also add a dashboard panel showing "key-variation-rate" (unique key variants / lookups) per-customer so this doesn't blindside us next time.
observability-bot: runbook note appended: if hit-rate delta > 10% for >30m and token_savings drop > 10k/day -> page eng-runtime on-call.
maria: i'll patch the dashboard to add the key-variation panel and share a short write-up in #eng-runtime after we confirm the fix. thx all :thumbsup:
sam: one more thing — if we add the shim, add an integration test that fuzzes whitespace/sep variants so key-normalizer regressions are caught in CI.
maria: added to action items. moving to followups.
